english.title: Asylum applicant failed to submit medical examination - immigration
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person in authorised detention at **(..SPECIFY..) detention centre and there being reasonable grounds for believing that you were suffering from a disease namely **(..SPECIFY..), specified in an order made by the Secretary of State, failed without reasonable excuse to submit to a medical examination having being required to do so by a detainee custody officer at that centre.
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 3(4) and (5) of Schedule 12 to the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being person in authorised detention
reasonable grounds to believe suffering from specified disease
without reasonable excuse
failed to submit to medical examination

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The medical examination must be conducted in accordance with detention centre rules (paragraph 3(3)).
(ii) 'Authorisation' means an authorisation given by the manager of the detention centre for the purposes of this paragraph (paragraph 3(6)).

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
